fragments.text: וְעִשָּׂר֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֑ד לְשִׁבְעַ֖ת הַכְּבָשִֽׂים׃
וּשְׂעִיר־עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֖ד חַטָּ֑את לְכַפֵּ֖ר עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
מִלְּבַד֩ עֹלַ֨ת הַחֹ֜דֶשׁ וּמִנְחָתָ֗הּ וְעֹלַ֤ת הַתָּמִיד֙ וּמִנְחָתָ֔הּ וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֖ם כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֑ם לְרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃
for each of the seven lambs.
And also one he-goat as a sin-offering to atone for you.

Apart from the whole-offering of the new moon and its meal-offering and the regular whole-offering with its meal-offering and their drink-offerings according to their rule for a sweet savour, a fire offering to the Lord.
וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
עַל־פִּי יְיָ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה:
עֵץ־חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ וְתוֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר:
דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־נֹעַם וְכָל־נְתִיבֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם:
אֹרֶךְ יָמִים בִּימִינָהּ בִּשְׂמֹאלָהּ עֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד:
יְיָ חָפֵץ לְמַעַן צִדְקוֹ יַגְדִּיל תּוֹרָה וְיַאְדִּיר:
This is the Torah which Moses placed before the Children of Israel
at the Lord’s command through Moses.
It is a tree of life for those who grasp it; and whoever supports it, is made happy.
Its ways are pleasant and all its paths are peace.
Length of days is in its right hand, in its left is wealth and honour.
The Lord delights for the sake of His righteousness to magnify the Torah and to glorify it.

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר בִּנְבִיאִים טוֹבִים וְרָצָה בְדִבְרֵיהֶם הַנֶּאֱמָרִים בֶּאֱמֶת בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַבּוֹחֵר בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ וּבִנְבִיאֵי הָאֱמֶת וָצֶדֶק:

Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has chosen worthy prophets and found pleasure in their words that are spoken in truth. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who has chosen the Torah and His servant Moses, His people Israel and prophets of truth and righteousness.

title.he: הפטרה ליום א׳ של ראש השנה

fragments.text: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד מִן־הָרָמָתַ֛יִם צוֹפִ֖ים מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמ֡וֹ אֶ֠לְקָנָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֧ם בֶּן־אֱלִיה֛וּא בֶּן־תֹּ֥חוּ בֶן־צ֖וּף אֶפְרָתִֽי׃
וְלוֹ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֔ים שֵׁ֚ם אַחַת֙ חַנָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פְּנִנָּ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י לִפְנִנָּה֙ יְלָדִ֔ים וּלְחַנָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין יְלָדִֽים׃
וְעָלָה֩ הָאִ֨ישׁ הַה֤וּא מֵעִירוֹ֙ מִיָּמִ֣ים יָמִ֔ימָה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֹ֥ת וְלִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּשִׁלֹ֑ה וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵי־עֵלִ֗י
חָפְנִי֙ וּפִנְחָ֔ס כֹּהֲנִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃
וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּזְבַּ֖ח אֶלְקָנָ֑ה וְנָתַ֞ן לִפְנִנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּֽלְכָל־בָּנֶ֛יהָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ מָנֽוֹת׃
וּלְחַנָּ֕ה יִתֵּ֥ן מָנָ֖ה אַחַ֣ת אַפָּ֑יִם כִּ֤י אֶת־חַנָּה֙ אָהֵ֔ב וַֽיהוָ֖ה סָגַ֥ר רַחְמָֽהּ׃
וְכִֽעֲסַ֤תָּה צָֽרָתָהּ֙ גַּם־כַּ֔עַס בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְּעִמָ֑הּ כִּֽי־סָגַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד רַחְמָֽהּ׃
וְכֵ֨ן יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה מִדֵּ֛י עֲלֹתָהּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֖ן תַּכְעִסֶ֑נָּה וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֹאכַֽל׃
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֜הּ אֶלְקָנָ֣ה אִישָׁ֗הּ חַנָּה֙ לָ֣מֶה תִבְכִּ֗י וְלָ֙מֶה֙ לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְלִ֔י וְלָ֖מֶה יֵרַ֣ע לְבָבֵ֑ךְ הֲל֤וֹא אָנֹכִי֙ ט֣וֹב לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃
וַתָּ֣קָם חַנָּ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְלָ֥הֿ בְשִׁלֹ֖ה וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁתֹ֑ה וְעֵלִ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֗ן יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־הַכִּסֵּ֔א עַל־מְזוּזַ֖ת הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃
וְהִ֖יא מָ֣רַת נָ֑פֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל עַל־יְהוָ֖ה וּבָכֹ֥ה תִבְכֶּֽה׃

וַתִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר וַתֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אִם־רָאֹ֥ה תִרְאֶ֣ה ׀ בָּעֳנִ֣י אֲמָתֶ֗ךָ וּזְכַרְתַּ֙נִי֙ וְלֹֽא־תִשְׁכַּ֣ח אֶת־אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ זֶ֣רַע אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּנְתַתִּ֤יו לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו וּמוֹרָ֖ה לֹא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃
וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י הִרְבְּתָ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְעֵלִ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֶת־פִּֽיהָ׃
וְחַנָּ֗ה הִ֚יא מְדַבֶּ֣רֶת עַל־לִבָּ֔הּ רַ֚ק שְׂפָתֶ֣יהָ נָּע֔וֹת וְקוֹלָ֖הּ לֹ֣א יִשָּׁמֵ֑עַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ עֵלִ֖י לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה׃
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ עֵלִ֔י עַד־מָתַ֖י תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִ֑ין הָסִ֥ירִי
אֶת־יֵינֵ֖ךְ מֵעָלָֽיִךְ׃
וַתַּ֨עַן חַנָּ֤ה וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲדֹנִ֔י אִשָּׁ֤ה קְשַׁת־ר֙וּחַ֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וְיַ֥יִן וְשֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
אַל־תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לִפְנֵ֖י בַּת־בְּלִיָּ֑עַל כִּ֥י מֵרֹ֥ב שִׂיחִ֛י וְכַעְסִ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃
וַיַּ֧עַן עֵלִ֛י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְכִ֣י לְשָׁל֑וֹם וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל יִתֵּן֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣לָתֵ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתְּ מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃
וַתֹּ֕אמֶר תִּמְצָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ הָאִשָּׁ֤ה לְדַרְכָּהּ֙ וַתֹּאכַ֔ל וּפָנֶ֥יהָ לֹא־הָֽיוּ־לָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃
וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־בֵּיתָ֣ם הָֽרָמָ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤דַע אֶלְקָנָה֙ אֶת־חַנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽזְכְּרֶ֖הָ יְהוָֽה׃
וַיְהִי֙ לִתְקֻפ֣וֹת הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתַּ֥הַר חַנָּ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמוֹ֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה שְׁאִלְתִּֽיו׃
וַיַּ֛עַל הָאִ֥ישׁ אֶלְקָנָ֖ה וְכָל־בֵּית֑וֹ לִזְבֹּ֧חַ לַיהוָ֛ה אֶת־זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֶת־נִדְרֽוֹ׃
וְחַנָּ֖ה לֹ֣א עָלָ֑תָה כִּֽי־אָמְרָ֣ה לְאִישָׁ֗הּ עַ֣ד־יִגָּמֵ֤ל הַנַּ֙עַר֙ וַהֲבִיאֹתִ֗יו וְנִרְאָה֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיָ֥שַׁב שָׁ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהּ֩ אֶלְקָנָ֨ה אִישָׁ֜הּ עֲשִׂ֧י הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינַ֗יִךְ שְׁבִי֙ עַד־גָּמְלֵ֣ךְ אֹת֔וֹ אַ֛ךְ יָקֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־דְּבָר֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וַתֵּ֣ינֶק אֶת־בְּנָ֔הּ עַד־גָמְלָ֖הּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
וַתַּעֲלֵ֨הוּ עִמָּ֜הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר גְּמָלַ֗תּוּ בְּפָרִ֣ים שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ וְאֵיפָ֨ה אַחַ֥ת קֶ֙מַח֙ וְנֵ֣בֶל יַ֔יִן וַתְּבִאֵ֥הוּ בֵית־יְהוָ֖ה
שִׁלֹ֑ו וְהַנַּ֖עַר נָֽעַר׃
וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת־הַפָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֥אוּ אֶת־הַנַּ֖עַר אֶל־עֵלִֽי׃
וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י חֵ֥י נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֲנִ֣י הָֽאִשָּׁ֗ה הַנִּצֶּ֤בֶת עִמְּכָה֙ בָּזֶ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃
אֶל־הַנַּ֥עַר הַזֶּ֖ה הִתְפַּלָּ֑לְתִּי וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ אֶת־שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתִּי מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃
וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֙הוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כָּל־הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֔ה ה֥וּא שָׁא֖וּל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ שָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָֽה׃
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל חַנָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר עָלַ֤ץ לִבִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה רָ֥מָה קַרְנִ֖י בַּֽיהוָ֑ה רָ֤חַב פִּי֙ עַל־א֣וֹיְבַ֔י כִּ֥י שָׂמַ֖חְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
אֵין־קָד֥וֹשׁ כַּיהוָ֖ה כִּי־אֵ֣ין בִּלְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר כֵּאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
אַל־תַּרְבּ֤וּ תְדַבְּרוּ֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה יֵצֵ֥א עָתָ֖ק מִפִּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל דֵּעוֹת֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְל֥א נִתְכְּנ֖וּ עֲלִלֽוֹת׃
קֶ֚שֶׁת גִּבֹּרִ֣ים חַתִּ֑ים וְנִכְשָׁלִ֖ים אָֽזְרוּ־חָֽיִל׃
שְׂבֵעִ֤ים בַּלֶּ֙חֶם֙ נִשְׂכָּ֔רוּ וּרְעֵבִ֖ים חָדֵ֑לוּ עַד עֲקָרָה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה שִׁבְעָ֔ה וְרַבַּ֥ת בָּנִ֖ים אֻמְלָֽלָה׃
יְהוָ֖ה מֵמִ֣ית וּמְחַיֶּ֑ה מוֹרִ֥יד שְׁא֖וֹל וַיָּֽעַל׃
יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִ֣ישׁ וּמַֽעֲשִׁ֑יר מַשְׁפִּ֖יל אַף־מְרוֹמֵֽם׃
מֵקִ֨ים מֵעָפָ֜ר דָּ֗ל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת֙ יָרִ֣ים אֶבְי֔וֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב֙ עִם־נְדִיבִ֔ים וְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד יַנְחִלֵ֑ם כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ מְצֻ֣קֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וַיָּ֥שֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם תֵּבֵֽל׃
רַגְלֵ֤י חֲסִידָו֙ יִשְׁמֹ֔ר וּרְשָׁעִ֖ים בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יִדָּ֑מּוּ כִּֽי־לֹ֥א בְכֹ֖חַ יִגְבַּר־אִֽישׁ׃
יְהוָ֞ה יֵחַ֣תּוּ
There was once a man from Romathaim-Tsofim, from the hill-country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah the son of Yeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Tsuf, an Efrathite.
He had two wives; the name of one was Hannah and that of the other was Peninah; Peninah had children but Hannah had no children.
This man used to go up from his town year by year to Shiloh in order to prostrate himself and to sacrifice before the Lord of Hosts. There were two sons of Eli, Hofni and Pinhas, priests to the Lord.
On
the day that Elkanah sacrificed, he used to give portions to his wife Peninah and to all her sons and daughters
but to Hannah he used to give a double portion because he loved Hannah even though the Lord had closed her womb.
Her rival used to annoy her by taunting her that the Lord had closed her womb.
He used to do this year by year and whenever she went up to the house of the Lord, her rival would annoy her so that she used to weep and would not eat.
Once her husband Elkanah said to her: ‘Hannah, why do you weep, why do you not eat and why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten children?’
Hannah arose after eating and drinking in Shiloh: and Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the Sanctuary of the Lord
when she in bitterness of soul prayed to the Lord and was weeping violently.

And she made a vow and said: ‘O Lord of Hosts, if Thou wilt only look at the misery of Thy handmaid and remember me and not forget Thy handmaid and give Thy handmaid a male child, I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life and no razor shall come upon his head’.
And it happened when she prayed so much before the Lord that Eli noticed her mouth.
For Hannah was talking to herself, only her lips were moving but her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought that she was drunk
and Eli said to her: ‘How much longer will you be drunk?
Remove your wine from yourself’.
Then Hannah answered saying: ‘It is not so, my lord; I am a woman with a heavy heart, I have drunk neither wine nor mead but I have poured out my soul before the Lord.
Do not consider your handmaid as a worthless woman for it is owing to the abundance of my grief and distress that I have spoken so long’.
Eli replied and said: ‘Go forth in peace and the God of Israel will grant your request which you asked of Him’.
She said: ‘May your handmaid find favour in your eyes’. Then the woman went her way, she ate and her face was no longer sad.
They rose early in the morning and prostrated themselves before the Lord, then they returned and arrived at their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew his wife Hannah and the Lord remembered her;
and in the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She called his name Samuel ‘for I have asked for him of the Lord’.
And the man Elkanah and the whole of his household went up to offer the annual sacrifice and his vow to the Lord.
Hannah, however, did not go up, for she said to her husband: ‘When the lad has been weaned, then I will bring him there that he may appear before the presence of the Lord and stay there for ever’.
Her husband Elkanah said to her: ‘Do what is best in your eyes, stay until you have weaned him; surely the Lord will fulfil His word’. The woman stayed and suckled her son until she had weaned him.
Then she brought him up with her after she had weaned him, together with three bullocks, one ephah of flour and one bottle of wine. She brought him into the House of the Lord
at Shiloh. The lad was still very young.
They slaughtered the bullock, and brought the lad to Eli.
She said: ‘I pray you, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here to pray to the Lord.
For this lad did I pray and the Lord granted my request for which I asked of Him.
I then dedicated him to the Lord; all the days that he exists, he is dedicated to the Lord’. Then he bowed down there before the Lord.
And Hannah prayed and said: ‘My heart has rejoiced in the Lord, my condition has been raised through the Lord; my mouth has triumphed over my enemies since I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.
None is holy as the Lord for there is none besides Thee and there is no rock like our God.
Do not continue to talk haughtily, let insolence leave your mouth for a God of knowledge is the Lord and to Him all deeds are known.
The bow of the mighty breaks and stumblers are girded with strength,
those once satisfied with food hire themselves out and the hungry cease to be hungry, even she who was childless has given birth to seven while another rich in children is forlorn.
The Lord slays and revives, brings down to the grave and raises up.
The Lord impoverishes and enriches, brings low and raises high,

lifting the poor from the dust and the needy from the dung-heap to seat them with nobles and endow them with a glorious throne, for the earth’s foundations are the Lord’s and He has placed the world upon them.
He guards the feet of his pious ones but evil doers are silenced in darkness for it is not by might that

head.he: הפטרה ליום א׳ של ראש השנה.

torah_s162_hagbah_intro_174.text: מי שברך. ומגביהין וגוללין. כשמגביהין הס״ת מביטין נגד הכתב של ס״ת ואומרין:

torah_s162_hagbah_intro_175.text: After the reading, the Torah scroll is lifted up and rolled together again. When the Torah scroll is being lifted up, one says:

torah_s162_haft_before_intro_174.text: קודם קריאת ההפטרה ואחר שנגמר הגולל, יברך המפטיר ברכה זו:

torah_haft_heading_he.text: הפטרה ליום א׳ של ראש השנה.
